mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.75% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.75% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% in a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day S&P 500 returns observed during four-month stretches of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation (stagflation risk), which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-mo moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in the housing sector, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-mo moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three-month stretches where HOUST exceeds its 6-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment falls while employment rises) above their 12-month averages in the same month signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-mo moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound; this anticipation of future demand lifts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six-month stretches where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).
